There are two MCDU's installed in the A320 on the pedestal for flight crew. They are used for loading and display of data. They enable the crew to interface with the FMGC by selection of a flight plan including its lateral/vertical trajectories and speed profiles. The crew can also modify any selected navigation or performance data within the MCDU. The MCDU also enables for specific functions of flight management such as, revising a flight plan, engine-out procedures, secondary flight plans etc.

The MCDU's also allow additional data such as Centralized Fault Display System (CFDS), ARINC Communication Addressing and Reporting System (ACARS), Air Traffic Service Unit (ATSU) and more to be accessed. Any data input into the MCDU, which is unallowable by the aircraft or beyond its capabilities, will automatically be disregarded or will generate an advisory message. When the RCL button is pressed, the E/WD displays:
*All warning, caution and status messages/pages that have been suppressed by the activation of the CLR button.
*All the alerts that are still active but inhibited in the whole active flight phase.

In case there are no suppressed warnings/cautions, the E/WD shows 'NORMAL' for 5 seconds. Pressing and holding the RCL button more than 3 seconds enables the E/WD to display to any caution messages that were suppressed by the EMER CANC button.

There are two MCDU's installed in the A320 on the pedestal for flight crew. They are used for loading and display of data. They enable the crew to interface with the FMGC by selection of a flight plan including its lateral/vertical trajectories and speed profiles. The crew can also modify any selected navigation or performance data within the MCDU. The MCDU also enables for specific functions of flight management such as, revising a flight plan, engine-out procedures, secondary flight plans etc.

The MCDU's also allow additional data such as Centralized Fault Display System (CFDS), ARINC Communication Addressing and Reporting System (ACARS), Air Traffic Service Unit (ATSU) and more to be accessed. Any data input into the MCDU, which is unallowable by the aircraft or beyond its capabilities, will automatically be disregarded or will generate an advisory message. Below is an image from the Airbus FCOM source showing the different keys on the MCDU.

The screen labeled 'ACTIVE' displays the frequency of the selected navaid, which can be identified by a green monitor light on the selection key. The screen labeled 'STBY/CRS' can be used to set up a secondary frequency, which can be made active by pressing the transfer key shown by the green double arrow symbol between these two displays. The frequency in this display can be changed via the circular white frequency selector knob underneath it.

As mentioned above, this button is used to transfer the frequency from the STBY display into the active one so the receiver can tune it. In simple terms, the button is used to interchange the ACTIVE and STBY frequencies.
When one of these is pressed (excluding the SEL Indicator):
*The ACTIVE window displays frequency set on that radio.
*The STBY/CRS window displays the selected standby frequency/course.
*The selected key illuminates a Green monitor light.

The SEL Indicator on both RMP's appears Amber when a transceiver which is normally associated with one RMP, is tuned by another. (For further info on this check the Airbus FCOM regarding whether 2 or 3 RMP's are installed).
If the aircraft is equipped with HF radios and an HF frequency is selected by the crew, this switch selects the AM mode as the default is SSB (Single-Side band mode).
These concentric knobs are used to select the STBY frequency or CRS. The outer knob controls the whole numbers whilst the inner one controls its decimal values e.g. 132.075.
The crew presses this button to select navigation receivers and courses through the RMP. It does not affect the normal communication radios and their respective frequencies.
The crew presses one of these keys to select a navigation radio to control through this RMP. The keys illuminate Green when pressed.
This switch controls the RMP's power supply.
Pressed: The related channel is elected for transmission and the three Green lines illuminate. If pressed again or another key pressed, then the channel is deselected.
CALL: Flashes Amber and a buzzer sounds when the SELCAL system detects a call.
MECH: Flashes Amber and a buzzer sounds when call is made from the nose gear bay. The MECH light goes off after 60 seconds if not reset.
ATT: Flashes Amber and a buzzer sounds when a call from a cabin crewmember is made. The ATT light goes off after 60 seconds if not reset.

Pressing and releasing these out selects the associated audio reception channel and its integral white light illuminates. Pressing the knob back in disconnects the associated reception channel and the light goes off. Rotating the knob adjusts the related volume.
This switch can operate as a press-to-talk button for boom mike or oxygen mask mike.

INT: The boom/mask mikes transmit on interphone regardless of which transmission key is selected. To gain reception on interphone, the crew must have INT selected and the INT reception knob pressed out.
Neutral: Reception is normal. Boom/mask mikes do not transmit in this case.
RAD (press + hold):
Boom/mask mikes transmit on the radio selected on the ACP.
ON VOICE Key
This key allows the crew to inhibit the audio navigation signals from beacons like the VOR/ADF. When pressed, the key filters out audio ident signals and Green light comes on.
SELCAL/RESET key
Pressing this button switches off the CALL, MECH and ATT lights.
The system includes a PA reception knob and a transmission key as seen.
The transmission key, when pressed and held

(Three Green lights come on), allows crew to make a PA announcement via either boom, mask or hand held mike. The reception knob, when pressed and released out allows the message to go through loudspeaker, and the integral white light illuminates. The knob can be turned to adjust volume.
When pressed in, the reception to the loudspeakers is disconnected and white lights go out.
The thrust levers are used for the following:
*Manually select engine thrust.
*Arm and activate the auto-thrust (A/THR).
*Engage reverse thrust.
*Engage the TOGA mode (Take Off and Go-Around).
When the auto thrust is inactive, the levers are used to control the thrust directly. Each levers
position corresponds to a given thrust setting including the set detents available and as shown in the image. These detents are as follows:
*TOGA: Maximum takeoff thrust.
body.label: TOGA

body.text: *FLX MCT: Maximum continuous thrust (or FLX at takeoff).
body.label: FLX MCT

On each lever handles sides are red instinctive sides are red instinctive auto thrust disconnect push buttons. Pressing these disconnects the auto thrust and the crew should first move the levers to match the current engine thrust level on the E/WD before disconnecting auto thrust.

On either side of the thrust levers are also the Pitch Trim Wheels. Both wheels provide mechanical control of the THS and have priority over electrical control. Manually moving it disconnects the autopilot. Before takeoff, the crew sets the THS to a value on the trims CG scale as calculated in the performance figures, which| are determined as a function of the aircraft CG. The limits of the THS normal setting for takeoff are indicated by a green band on the pitch trim wheel.
In flight, when in direct law, the crew uses the THS conventionally to fly in trim. In flight, the aircraft pitch trim setting depends on the CG, weight, altitude and speed.

On landing, once the nose wheel touches down, as the pitch attitude becomes less than 2.5° for more than 5 seconds, the pitch trim automatically resets to zero. (Not operative if green or yellow hydraulic system not pressurized).
The switch sets the radar to ON (1 or 2) or OFF.
In a case where only one radar is installed on the aircraft then:
-An "INOP" or "DEACT"
label replaces the "2", or
-An "ON/OFF" Radar switch replaces the
"1/OFF/2" switch.
In the above case, weather returns are only displayed on the ND when switch is set to "1".
Display Mode Selector
WX (Weather Mode) Colors indicate the intensity of the weather returns/precipitation.
(Black for the lowest intensity, green, amber and red indicate higher intensities).
The ND shows precipitation and turbulence areas. Turbulence is displayed in | magenta (within 40nm).
Radar operates in ground mapping mode. Black indicates water, green indicates ground and amber indicates cities/mountains.
Adjusts the antenna tilt above/below the horizon. Zero indicates the horizon reference, as supplied by the ADIRS.
Used to adjust the sensitivity of the radar. In AUTO mode, the radar automatically adjusts the gain to the optimum setting.
AUTO: This activates the predictive windshear
function. Such areas can be detected when radio height is below 1500 feet, even if the radar switch is set to OFF.
OFF: Turns off the predictive windshear function.
OFF - weather data is not displayed on the related ND display. If the WXR/PWS switch is not set to OFF, the Predictive Windshear (PWS) function is active during takeoff and landing.
ALL WX - ND shows the ON PATH and OFF PATH weather. PWS and Turbulence display are also available.
PATH WX - ND shows ON PATH weather only. PWS and Turbulence display are also available.
ELEVN - ND shows the weather data at a selected altitude only via use of the ELEVN knob. PWS and Turbulence display are also available.
MAP - ND only shows ground echoes. PWS
display is available but Turbulence and HZD function are not available
When the display mode selector is set to ELEVN, the crew can use this knob to rotate and set the altitude or Flight level of the weather return to be shown on the ND.
The switch turns one radar to ON or turns off both radars.
Note:
*If only one radar is installed, a DEACT label is placed next to the 2 label to indicate system 2 is deactivated.
*When radar is switched ON, a 30 second delay occurs before weather is displayed. This is the time needed to scan the entire volume ahead of the aircraft for the first time.
*The Predictive Windshear (PWS) detection is available as soon as radar is set to ON and activation conditions are satisfied.
TURB and HZD mode selection

TURB button - during normal operation, the TURB function is active (TURB light illuminated on). The crew can remove the turbulence display from the ND (e.g. for de-cluttering purposes) by pushing the TURB button again (light off). Turbulence zones are shown in Magenta color on the ND (within 60 NM).
HZD button - This shows the hail and lightning zones on the ND. In normal operations, the HZD
function is active (HZD button light on). The crew can remove the HZD icon displays from the ND (e.g. for de-cluttering purposes) by pushing the HZD button again (light off).

This knob allows adjusting of the sensitivity of the radar around a certain calibrated position (AUTO). The crew can manually adjust the gain of the weather radar display using the knob. Normally this should be set to AUTO.
ON
When ON, the LP fuel valve opens (provided engine fire push-button is in).
During an automatic start sequence, the HP fuel valve opens if:
*The ENG MODE selector is set to IGN/START.
*N2 is above the following threshold: 22% on the ground and 15% in flight.
During a manual start, the HP fuel valve opens if:
*The ENG MODE selector is set to IGN/START.
*The MAN START push-button is ON.
OFF
When OFF, close signals are sent directly to the HP and LP fuel valves. These signals cause both FADEC channels to be reset.
Amber light illuminates and an ECAM Caution appears if:
*There is an automatic start abort.
*There is disagreement between the HP fuel valve position and its commanded position.
This light indicates the engine to be shut down in case of a fire. It appears in Red when an engine fire warning is triggered.
CRANK
Start valves open if the MAN START button is ON. Ignition does not fire.
NORM
Turns on continuous ignition (A and B) when the engine is running and either when a flameout is detected or an EIU fails.
IGN/START
If Master switch is on and N2 ≥ idle, this position selects continuous ignition (A and B):
*During an automatic start on the ground, when N2 passes 16%, ignition switches to A or B. Note that if there is an ignition delay during start sequence, ignition is continuous.
*In flight, continuous ignition begins when the MATER switch is set to ON.
On the ground, ignition shuts off automatically at the end of a start sequence when N * 2 > 50% The pack valves close automatically during a start sequence.

When ON, all intruders are displayed and in AUTO only proximate and other intruders are displayed, if a TA or RA is already presented. Some Panels indicate this switch with THRT/ALL and the associated functions remain the same. STBY puts the system in standby mode.
Selects ATC transponder 1 or 2.
ABV: The altitude range is set to +7000 ft above the aircraft and -2700 ft below.
N: Neutral position sets range to ±2700 ft.
BLW: The altitude range is set to -7000 ft below the aircraft and +2700 ft above.
Keyboard
Crew uses these push buttons to set the transponder code assigned by ATC or the relevant emergency codes such as 7700 (emergency), 7600 (radio/com failure) and 7500 (hijack).
Clears the code display.
ATC FAIL
Light comes on if the selected transponder 1 or 2 fails.
This window displays the selected code.
The crew presses this to send an aircraft identification signal to ATC.
STBY
Both ATC transponders and TCAS are electronically supplied, but stay on standby.
ALT RPTG OFF
No altitude data is transmitted.
XPNDR

In flight, the selected ATC transponder operates in all modes and the aircraft barometric data is also transmitted. ATC 1 uses ADR 1 or 3 and ATC 2 uses ADR 2 or 3. The TCAS in this case remains on standby.
On the ground, the selected ATC transponder only operates in mode S (Selective aircraft interrogation mode).
TA ONLY

Used in case of degraded aircraft performance issues such as, engine failures, landing gear extended, or approach on parallel runways. All RA's are converted into TA's. The display shows TA's, proximate and other intruders.
TA/RA
This is the normal position. TA's, RA's, proximate and other intruders are all displayed.

The lever controls the position of the speed brake surfaces. As you move the lever down, the surfaces extend by a certain value and there is even a 1⁄2 way mark indicate along the scale. In the A320, extending the speed brakes with autopilot on is limited to only half value despite full down position. When the lever is pulled up from its top position (RET); this action arms the ground spoilers. During landing or rejected takeoff (> 70 knots), when the spoilers are armed like this they automatically deploy or when reverse thrust is selected.

controls.name: RUD TRIM Rotary switch/Reset button/Position Indicator

body.text: The rotary switch controls the rudder trim actuator, which moves the neutral point of the artificial feel by an equivalent of one degree of rudder travel per second. The rotary switch has no effect if the Autopilot is engaged.

The RESET button to its left orders the Zero trim position at 1.5°/s. After pressing the RESET, an indication of up to 0.3° (L or R) may be seen in the position indicator above it. The button is non-active when AP is engaged.
The Position indication above the RESET button displays the rudder trim direction (L or R) and the relevant value (0 - 20°).

controls.name: Cockpit Door Toggle switch + Fault light

body.text: UNLOCK: Enables cabin crew to open the door when the switch is pushed and maintained in this position.
NORM: All latches are locked, and only emergency access is possible for cabin crew.
LOCK: In this position the door is locked. Emergency access, the buzzer and the keypad are inhibited for a preselected period (5-20 minutes).
-If the pilots have not used the LOCK position for at least 5 to 20 minutes, the cabin crew can request emergency access to open the door.
-The UNLOCK position overrides and resets any previous selections made by crew.
- If there is an electrical supply failure, the cockpit door is automatically unlocked, but remains closed.
OPEN Light ON: Door is not closed/locked.
OPEN Light flashing: Cabin crew is commencing the emergency access procedure. If the pilots don't react then the door will unlock at the end of the adjustment delay period (15 to 120 seconds).
FAULT Light: A failure has been detected in the cockpit door system.
Printer
Prints reports from the following systems (if installed) via the MCDU: ACARS, AIDS, FMGC, CFDIU and EVMU.
Pulling this handle and turning it clockwise to ON sets the parking brake. An ECAM memo displays 'PARK BRK'. If the pointer is not at ON, then the brake is OFF.

The crew can pull the gear crank out and turn it clockwise for 3 turns to extend the landing gear using gravity. Operating this handle, the cutout valve shuts off hydraulic pressure to the landing gear system and depressurizes it.
